headline: Isla Verde ferry link restored after five-year closure
subheadline: The first scheduled crossing since 2021 carried 300 passengers, many of them islanders returning to visit relatives.
description: A passenger ferry between Isla Verde and the mainland has resumed service after a five-year closure caused by storm damage to the island's harbour.
author: a-rossi

image.alt: A small passenger ferry moored at a harbour quay
image.caption: A passenger ferry at a harbour quay (file photo). The restored Isla Verde service will run twice daily.
image.credit: Photo: Ciara Ní Riain / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

seo.title: Isla Verde ferry link restored after five-year closure
seo.description: The Isla Verde passenger ferry has resumed service for the first time since storm damage closed the island's harbour in 2021.

body: ISLA VERDE — Cheers greeted the first scheduled ferry to dock at Isla Verde's harbour in five years on Friday morning, marking the end of a closure that had cut the island off from regular passenger services since a winter storm destroyed its breakwater in 2021.

The rebuilt harbour includes a higher breakwater, a floating pontoon designed to cope with larger tidal ranges and a small passenger terminal. Construction was repeatedly delayed by funding disputes and two further storm seasons.

For most of the closure, islanders depended on a small air shuttle and occasional cargo boats. Residents said the cost of travel had pushed younger families to leave, and the island's population fell by almost a fifth.

body.text: My grandchildren have never been able to just come for the weekend. Today they are on that boat.
body.cite: Isla Verde resident, speaking at the harbour

body: The service will initially run twice daily, increasing to four crossings in summer. The operator says it expects demand from tourists keen to visit the island's recently mapped deep-sea coral reef, which scientists described last month.
Isla Verde will host the next Coastal Cities Alliance summit in 2027.
